contract_binding.rule: Any contract or baseline movement invalidates this plan and requires a new review.

root_cause.failure: Chat HTTP and SSE append a user message and invoke the lifecycle graph without a durable external request identity.
proof: ChatRequest has no client_request_id while structured transaction requests already require one.
ConversationTurnService appends the user message before any durable request claim in both chat and stream paths.
StoreProvider has no TurnRequestRepository and MessageRepository has no stable message_id argument.
The frontend creates a request ID for the optimistic user row but does not send that ID to /chat/turn.

scope_amendment.reason: The frozen contract requires the user message to carry TurnRequestLedger.message_id, but its initial implementation_scope omitted the concrete SQLite message store and AgentService composition seam.
scope_amendment.rule: These paths are not writable until the implementation plan review explicitly approves this amendment.

phases.name: Repository types and deterministic digest
requirements: Define immutable TurnRequestScope, TurnRequestClaim and claim-decision types.
Canonicalize request digest from normalized message, trusted actor context and response profile; exclude transport.
Do not import LangGraph, model clients or API schemas into the repository layer.
tests: first claim creates one turn_id and message_id
same key and different digest conflicts
phases.rollback: Remove the new repository module and protocol additions; no existing storage behavior changes in this phase.

phases.name: SQLite atomic claim and fenced completion
requirements: Use one composite unique key for tenant, user, thread and client_request_id.
Claim with BEGIN IMMEDIATE or an equivalent atomic transaction.
Use monotonically increasing fencing tokens and owner-bound compare-and-set transitions.
Expired RUNNING returns recovery-required; it never silently becomes a new execution.
phases.rollback: Stop wiring the repository in StoreProvider; retain an unused table rather than destructive rollback.

phases.name: SQLAlchemy and PostgreSQL parity
requirements: Define the same composite uniqueness and record fields as SQLite.
Implement transactional insert-or-read claim and fenced compare-and-set completion.
Schema-present mode must fail clearly when the required table/columns are absent; it may not create production schema implicitly.
tests: schema-present validation catches missing ledger table
concurrent insert-or-read yields one authoritative record
phases.rollback: Disable provider exposure of turn_requests; do not weaken production schema validation.

phases.name: Stable message identity
requirements: MessageRepository.add_message accepts an optional stable message_id.
User-message insert is idempotent under tenant/user/thread/message identity.
Existing historical rows remain readable and assistant-message persistence remains backward compatible.
A duplicate message_id with different public content fails closed.
tests: different content under same identity conflicts
legacy messages without stable ID remain readable
phases.rollback: Callers stop passing message_id; optional columns remain non-authoritative and backward compatible.

phases.name: Chat API and service composition
requirements: ChatRequest.client_request_id is required and non-empty.
AgentService receives TurnRequestRepository from StoreProvider; it does not construct a second repository.
ChatPanel generates one request ID, uses it for the optimistic user row and sends the same value as client_request_id.
The server does not generate a public chat request ID fallback.
tests: missing ID is rejected at API boundary
frontend sends optimistic-row ID as client_request_id
phases.rollback: Revert the API/frontend phase together; do not make the field optional as compatibility fallback.

phases.name: HTTP and SSE orchestration integration
requirements: Claim after authenticated scope and conversation lease, before message append or graph access.
NEW_CLAIM alone may append the user message and invoke the graph.
REPLAY_SUCCEEDED returns or emits the stored canonical ChatResponse without graph/model invocation.
PAYLOAD_CONFLICT, REQUEST_IN_PROGRESS and RECOVERY_REQUIRED are typed fail-closed responses.
Both HTTP and SSE pass ledger turn_id/message_id into trace and graph input without creating a second semantic authority.
tests: same ID HTTP retry invokes graph once
HTTP then SSE with same ID uses one turn
SSE disconnect retry replays terminal response
phases.rollback: Revert orchestration and API/frontend phases together; leave repositories unused rather than bypassing the ledger.

phases.name: Crash boundary and response durability
requirements: Persist canonical public response before SUCCEEDED transition and successful return.
Complete with owner, fencing token, digest and expected state compare-and-set.
A crash after claim, message append, graph completion or response persistence has a separately tested recovery decision.
Unknown completion never automatically invokes the graph again.
tests: crash after message append does not append twice
crash after graph completion reconciles authoritative checkpoint/response
stale worker cannot overwrite recovered success
phases.rollback: Disable the chat endpoint rather than allowing uncertain automatic re-execution.

phases.name: Regression, diff review and baseline refresh
requirements: Run focused repository, concurrency, API, HTTP/SSE and crash tests.
Run full Agent, Business, frontend and lifecycle canary quick profile.
Independent Diff Integrity Reviewer verifies no message/graph path bypasses the ledger.
Only after diff approval, a separate control-plane operation refreshes product-source-baseline.json.
Closure Arbiter requires all 13 contract acceptance tests plus complete regression evidence.
phases.rollback: Revert the complete WP-02 implementation commit set and restore the previously validated B30 tree.

review_questions: Does the scope amendment for AgentService and MessageStore follow necessarily from the frozen message identity invariant?
Can any path append a user message or invoke the graph before a successful ledger claim?
Can an expired or uncertain record cause automatic re-execution?
Are HTTP and SSE using one transport-neutral identity and stored result?
Can a stale worker complete with an obsolete fencing token?
Does any implementation phase reuse action IdempotencyStore as conversational authority?
Is product-source baseline refresh performed by a separate control-plane actor after diff approval?
permit_preconditions: tests and rollback bound in ChangePermit
